purpose: Test whether inferred U<->D orientation transitions repeatedly align with present-day niche shifts on branches, without requiring an absolute dated tree.

input_contract.taxon_gate: same frozen FDT4 primary gate: >=10 independent thinned environment-complete occurrences per resolved U/D taxon
input_contract.tree_source: first six AU-nonrejected Comp1061 optimized topologies

method.discrete_trait: symmetric two-state CTMC estimated separately on each topology; edge U->D and D->U probabilities are retained rather than forcing one ancestral state
method.continuous_niche: Brownian squared-change ancestral reconstruction on relative branch lengths using standardized taxon niche centroids
method.directional_statistic: transition-probability-weighted branch niche shift, signed so positive values mean the D direction is associated with higher niche values
method.null: 499 tip-state permutations preserving the observed 5 U / 4 D counts, refitting the CTMC for each permutation
method.claim_boundary: Exploratory branchwise concordance screen. Relative branch lengths are sufficient for this directionality test, but absolute event timing, historical range, adaptation and ecological causation are not tested.

chelsa_bio15.direction: U_to_D aligned with higher precipitation seasonality

chelsa_bio01.direction: U_to_D aligned with lower annual mean temperature

interpretation.supported: The branchwise direction matches the earlier present-day PGLS on all six accepted topologies: D-direction changes align with higher BIO15 and lower BIO1. The signal therefore is not only a terminal-state mean difference.
interpretation.not_supported_yet: Neither branchwise concordance reaches the frozen exploratory permutation threshold. The evidence is directional and topology-stable, but not yet sufficient to claim repeated niche-associated convergence.
interpretation.main_bottleneck: taxon coverage rather than topology: two Taiwan taxa (Cirsium morii and Cirsium tatakaense) each have n=9 and remain one independent thinned occurrence below the primary gate.

next_decision: Keep BIO15 as the primary niche axis and BIO1 as the secondary axis for the next branchwise test. First increase morii and tatakaense to the frozen n>=10 gate; then rerun the same six-topology branchwise concordance before adding any dated-event model.
